identity.title: Structural Integrity Of "A" Train Service Water Header Piping Could Not Be Demonstrated Causing The Unit To Operate In A Condition Prohibited By Technical Specifications

cause.proximate_text: The cause of degradation was internal liner failure which allowed seawater to come in contact with ductile cast iron piping and led to corrosion. Additionally, previous internal inspections on this piping did not identify this potential failure mode.
cause.theme: internal liner failure leading to seawater-induced corrosion of ductile cast iron piping, undetected by prior inspections

nodes.display_name: Corrosion of ductile cast iron piping
nodes.description: Seawater contact with exposed cast iron led to corrosion developing over time.
Corrosion progressed to a through-wall flaw (~6 dpm leak) in the 24"-KE-1 piping, masked externally by the liner.

nodes.display_name: Previous internal inspections failed to detect liner/piping degradation
nodes.description: Previous internal inspections on this piping did not identify this potential failure mode, allowing the degradation to go undetected across the operating cycle.

nodes.display_name: Structural integrity of 'A' Train Service Water header piping could not be demonstrated; unit operated in a condition prohibited by Technical Specifications

properties.note: Loss of structural integrity existed longer than the 72-hour TS allowed outage time; no actual leakage/safety consequence occurred; low potential safety significance
